facts.statement: Germanodactylus is a genus of pterodactyloid pterosaur from the Upper Jurassic of Germany, including the Solnhofen Limestone.
facts.quote: Germanodactylus ("German finger") is a genus of germanodactylid pterodactyloid pterosaur from Upper Jurassic-age rocks of Germany, including the Solnhofen Limestone.

facts.statement: A distinctive head crest is a key feature of Germanodactylus.
facts.quote: The head crest of Germanodactylus is a distinctive feature.

facts.statement: The type species G. cristatus is based on specimen BSP 1892.IV.1 found in the Solnhofen limestone of Eichstätt, Germany.
facts.quote: G. cristatus is based on specimen BSP 1892.IV.1, from the Solnhofen limestone of Eichstätt, Germany.

facts.statement: Carl Wiman named the species G. cristatus in 1925, deriving the name from the Latin word for "crested".
facts.quote: It was originally described by Plieninger in 1901 as a specimen of Pterodactylus kochi, and was given its current specific name by Carl Wiman in 1925, meaning "crested" in Latin.

facts.statement: Yang Zhongjian elevated the species to its own genus, Germanodactylus, in 1964.
facts.quote: Yang Zhongjian determined that it deserved its own genus in 1964.

facts.statement: The species G. rhamphastinus was originally described by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1851 as a species of the genus Ornithocephalus.
facts.quote: A second species called G. ramphastinus (in 1858 accidentally revised to rhamphastinus by Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer) was named as a distinct species long before G. cristatus, described by Johann Andreas Wagner in 1851 as a species of the now deprecated genus Ornithocephalus.

facts.statement: The species G. rhamphastinus is based on specimen BSP AS.I.745, a skeleton from the Mörnsheimer Limestone of Daiting, Germany.
facts.quote: It is based on specimen BSP AS.I.745, a skeleton from the slightly younger Mörnsheimer Limestone of Daiting, Germany.

facts.statement: Peter Wellnhofer included G. rhamphastinus in the genus Germanodactylus in 1970.
facts.quote: Peter Wellnhofer added it to Germanodactylus in 1970

facts.statement: David M. Unwin referred limb bones and vertebrae from the Kimmeridge Clay of Dorset, England, to the genus Germanodactylus.
facts.quote: David M. Unwin has also referred miscellaneous limb bones and vertebrae from the somewhat older Kimmeridge Clay of Dorset, England to the genus

facts.statement: G. cristatus has no teeth at the jaw tip and fewer teeth than G. rhamphastinus, which has approximately 16 upper and 15 lower teeth per side.
facts.quote: G. cristatus differs from "G. rhampastinus" by having no teeth in the tip of the jaw and fewer teeth (~13 in each side of the upper jaw and ~12 in the lower versus 16 upper and 15 lower on each side for "G. rhamphastinus").

facts.statement: G. cristatus had a 0.98-meter wingspan and a 13-centimeter skull, while G. rhamphastinus had a 1.08-meter wingspan and a 21-centimeter skull.
facts.quote: G. cristatus had a 0.98 meter wingspan (3.2 ft) and a 13 centimeter (5.1 in) long skull, while "G. rhamphastinus" was somewhat larger, with a 1.08 meter (3.5 ft) wingspan, and a skull measuring 21 centimeters (8.3 in) long.

facts.statement: A tentatively referred hindlimb suggests that G. cristatus may have reached sizes larger than the known specimens.
facts.quote: A pterosaur hindlimb tentatively referred to G. cristatus suggests the species may have reached even larger sizes.

facts.statement: The soft-tissue component of the head crest was first described in 2002 by S. Christopher Bennett.
facts.quote: The soft-tissue portion was not known early on, being first described in 2002 by S. Christopher Bennett.

facts.statement: The soft-tissue portion of the crest was probably composed of cornified epidermis.
facts.quote: It was probably composed of cornified epidermis.

facts.statement: Germanodactylus is the first genus known to have a soft-tissue component of its crest, though similar structures were likely widespread among pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Germanodactylus is the first genus for which a soft-tissue component of the crest is known, but similar structures were probably widespread among pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Yang Zhongjian established the family Germanodactylidae for the genus.
facts.quote: Yang Zhongjian, who named the genus, gave it its own family Germanodactylidae.

facts.statement: Bennett placed the genus in the family Pterodactylidae, while Alexander W.A. Kellner found it related to Pterodactylus in his 2003 analysis.
facts.quote: Bennett included the genus in the family Pterodactylidae, and Alexander W.A. Kellner found it to be related to Pterodactylus in his 2003 phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: In 2017, Vidovic and Martill created the new genus Altmuehlopterus for G. rhamphastinus.
facts.quote: However, in a subsequent paper published in 2017, Vidovic and Martill created a new genus for "G. rhamphastinus", Altmuehlopterus.

facts.statement: Germanodactylus lived in what is now Germany during the Upper Jurassic and was discovered in Solnhofen Limestone rocks.
facts.quote: Germanodactylus (gr. "dedo alemán") es un género de pterosaurios pterodactiloideos que vivieron en lo que hoy es Alemania durante el Jurásico Superior, siendo descubierto en rocas de la Caliza de Solnhofen.

facts.statement: The beak was long and narrow with few or no teeth; the teeth were short and peg-like, but absent at the tip, which instead had a horny extension.
facts.quote: El pico era largo y estrecho con pocos o sin dientes; de sus dientes eran cortos en forma de clavija, pero en el extremo del pico no tenía; en lugar de ellos tenía un extremo córneo.

facts.statement: It is debated whether G. rhamphastinus deserves its own genus, "Daitingopterus", as suggested by Maisch and coauthors.
facts.quote: Maisch and his coauthors have suggested that it deserves its own genus, "Daitingopterus".

facts.statement: Bennett suggested in 1996 that Germanodactylus represented adults of Pterodactylus, but this hypothesis was later rejected by further studies.
facts.quote: Bennett suggested in 1996 that Germanodactylus represented adults of Pterodactylus, but this has been rejected by further studies, including his own.

facts.statement: The first fossils, impressions of the animal in limestone, were discovered in 1892.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles, impresiones del animal en piedra caliza, se descubrieron en 1892.

facts.statement: G. cristatus is known from four specimens including two juveniles.

facts.statement: The genus differs from other pterosaurs by a combination of features including a pointed jaw tip, 4 to 5 premaxillary teeth, and 8 to 12 maxillary teeth on each side of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: El género difiere de otros pterosaurios por una combinación de características incluyendo una mandíbula terminada en punta, 4 a 5 dientes premaxilares y 8 a 12 dientes maxilares a cada lado de la mandíbula superior

facts.statement: It is classified in the class Reptilia.
